summary: A scholar in religious studies and Indology, Albertus Bruining studied at the University of Amsterdam (~1864–1868) and Leiden University (~1868–1871, Dr.theol.) under Johan Hendrik Caspar Kern and Paul Deussen. In 1900, he became Professor of Theology at Amsterdam.

Albertus Wilhelmus van den Hoek was an Indologist who studied at the University of Amsterdam (~1968–1969) and Leiden University (B.A. ~1970, M.A. ~1976), learning under Jan C. Heesterman and Louis Dumont. He served as head at Leiden University (1989–1992).
Working in Indology and other fields, Albinas Rimka taught economics at Vytautas Magnus University (1923–1925) and at Vilnius University (1940).

A scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies, Butters earned degrees from UC Santa Cruz, Harvard, and Columbia, studying with Robert A. F. Thurman and others. He was an Adjunct Lecturer at the University of Turku (2013–2020) and Editor at Khyentse Vision Project (2021).

Albrecht Hanisch, an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar, completed his doctoral degree at the University of Marburg under Michael Hahn in 2000. He later served as Acting Director of the Nepal Research Centre and Local Representative for the Nepalese-German Manuscript Cataloguing Project.

Albrecht Weber was an Indologist and linguist who earned his doctorate from Breslau and studied at Bonn and Berlin under Adolf Friedrich Stenzler, Christian Lassen, Johann Gildemeister, and Adalbert Kuhn. He held teaching posts at Humboldt University of Berlin (1848–1901).

Indologist and philosopher Albrecht Wezler earned his Dr. phil. at Tübingen (~1960–1965) under Paul Thieme. He served as Director at the University of Hamburg (1973–2003), Director of the Nepal Research Centre (1982–2004), and Director General of the Nepal-German Manuscript Preservation Project (1982–2002).

Aleix Ruiz-Falqués, an Indologist, linguist, and Buddhist studies scholar, earned his PhD at the University of Cambridge under Eivind Kahrs by 2016. He has held positions at Shan State Buddhist University, Singapore University of Technology and Design, and the Pali Text Society.

Aleksander Brückner worked in linguistics, history, and archaeology. He studied at Lviv, Vienna, and Berlin under August Leskien, and held posts at the University of Lviv (~1878–1881) and Frederick William University Berlin (~1881–1924).

Aleksander Dunin Borkowski was an Indology scholar who studied at Chernivtsi University (1827), the University of Lviv (~1828–1832), and the University of Königsberg (~1833–1835) under Peter von Bohlen.

Freiman was an Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar and linguist. He studied at Saint Petersburg and Giessen under Christian Bartholomae, Carl Salemann, Sergey Oldenburg, and others. He served at Saint Petersburg State University from 1917, holding the Iranian philology chair (1938–1950).

Aleksandr Gilferding was a scholar of linguistics and Indology who completed his master's dissertation at Moscow State University (1852–1853) under Viktor Grigorovich. He worked at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (1853) and served as President of the Russian Geographical Society (~1870–1872).

Linguist Aleksandr Ivanovich Aleksandrov studied at Kazan State University under Jan Niecisław Baudouin de Courtenay and Mikołaj Kruszewski, and at Tartu. He was Professor at the University of Kharkiv (1886), Kazan State University (1888–1911), and Kazan Theological Academy (1912).

Aleksandr Ivanovich Tomson was a linguist who studied at Saint Petersburg State University (1882–1887) under Filipp Fedorovich Fortunatov and Theodor Korsch. He served as ordinary Professor of Indo-European Linguistics and Sanskrit at Odesa University from 1897 to 1932.

Aleksandr Leonovič Grjunberg-Cvetinovič was a scholar of linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. He studied at Saint Petersburg State University under Ivan Ivanovich Zarubin, later holding posts at the University (1964–1995) and the Institute for Linguistic Studies (~1960–1995).

Linguist Aleksandr Lvovich Duvernois studied at Moscow State University (1855–1866) under Pavel Jakovlevič Petrov. He later served as Professor of Comparative Linguistics at Moscow State University (~1869–1886).

Aleksandr Mervart was an Indologist and linguist who earned his Ph.D. at Heidelberg University (~1904–1907). He worked at the Kunstkamera (from 1913; Keeper 1924–1930) and taught at Saint Petersburg State University (1924–1930).

Aleksandr Mikhailovich Osipov was an Indologist and historian who studied at Moscow State University (~1922–1926). He taught at the Moscow Institute of Oriental Studies (1926–1935) and held the chair of Indian History at Moscow State University (1936).

Aleksandr Semënovič Zimin was an Indologist who studied under Fyodor Shcherbatskoy in 1920. He was a Docent at the Leningrad Oriental Institute in 1934 and worked at the Institute of Oriental Manuscripts of the Russian Academy of Sciences in 1937.
Aleksandr Vasil'yevich Popov was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Kupiansk Theological Seminary (1871–1875) and subsequently studied under Vincenz Scherzl (~1875–1879).
